study: Locally fixed secondary diagnostic on previously inspected PMLB tasks, archived proposals and known XGBoost results; no public preregistration or outcome-dependent choice among configurations.
population: All 42 frozen folds and all 704 distinct fold-support pairs in the refit-target archive. Report the 400 search-path and 379 uniform-deletion memberships separately, retaining their overlap. Use exactly the archived anchor and train/rank/test split, class order and nonempty supports for both learners.
vote: Use paired rank-panel AUC and accuracy for the masked anchor and masked support with each common restored context. Keep the rare-positive AP allowance fixed at 5 percent in every cell. A yes vote requires all metric losses <= relative allowance times absolute reference score + 1e-12. For minimum, every context's fraction of yes votes must meet the quorum. For pooled, the fraction of all context-panel ballots must meet that same quorum. Retain equivalences due to finite panel counts and endpoint-only families. Empty and endpoints use at most the two distinct endpoint contexts.
panel_generation: Reuse the archived ranking-panel sample, class masses, and exactly the original 4 weight vectors. Append 8 independent stratified resampling vectors on the same ranking rows, with numpy SeedSequence([20421+fold,659,8181]); retain sampled class size and original ranking-pool class mass. Use first 1/4/12 vectors of this nested list, paired across masks, configurations, and learners. These are repeated weights on the same rows, not new observations.

learners.xgb: Frozen primary CPU histogram XGBoost (100 rounds, depth 4, learning rate .1, one thread). Reconstruct the full fitted masking model and vote arrays; assert original 4-panel, 3-percent cells and 8 archived decisions agree on every support. Rescore archived hashed outer XGBoost anchor/support probabilities and verify all archived fixed-target labels.
learners.logistic: Fixed L2 logistic regression with C=1, lbfgs, tol=1e-4, max_iter=2000, intercept, no class weights or tuning. Median impute then standardize using fitting rows only for the full masking predictor and all development rows for outer refits. Use the same raw median masking reference as XGBoost, transformed using the corresponding full model scaler. Independently fit the same regularized logistic model on A and each S using all development rows and score outer test rows; fixed early XGBoost-supplied supports/contexts are not regenerated for logistic. Record convergence warnings.

target: Two separate learner-specific binary outer outcomes, always fixed at 3 percent relative loss in AUC or accuracy (and 5 percent relative AP for rare positives), epsilon=1e-12. Evaluate XGBoost votes against XGBoost refits and logistic votes against logistic refits as the primary pairs. Report both crossed pairs separately as transfer diagnostics. Never substitute a vote-side threshold into the outer target.
analysis: Preserve every rule for each learner pair. Primary reference: separating minimum, strict majority over four panels, 3 percent vote allowance. Compare this to endpoints, random, pooled, 1 and 12 panels, quorum alternatives, and 1/5 percent tolerances by changing one setting at a time. Report TP FP FN TN, sensitivity, specificity and the percentages of all proposals that are TP and FP. Pooled counts and equal-task rates (average proposal indicators within fold, then folds within task, then tasks equally) are descriptive. For conditional equal-task sensitivity/specificity use the ratios of these equal-task joint rates. Report per-task fold-averaged joint rates and cohort overlaps; no independent proposal inference, thresholds fitted on outcomes, or universal winner.
execution: Hash the design, analysis code, donor protocol and fold inputs before new computations. Freeze new votes before opening outer predictions. One thread per learner, one-hour maximum per fold, record every failed fold or warning. Report missing folds explicitly. Complete all predeclared successful cells and do not change operating points in response to findings.
